title: Microsoft 365 Education Is Evolving: What Education Leaders Need to Know
summary: Microsoft 365 Education is changing. Learn about the new A0 and A7 editions, storage updates, and legacy offer retirements so you can plan ahead.
body_markdown:
AI is reshaping how students learn, how educators teach, and how institutions operate. Education IT leaders must also protect data, secure identities and devices, control costs, and prepare for responsible AI. Microsoft is responding with one of the most significant updates to the Microsoft 365 Education portfolio in more than a decade.


The updated portfolio introduces new faculty and student editions, greater flexibility to mix licenses, options with or without Teams, expanded security and management value, and a clearer path for institutions ready to operationalize AI. For education leaders, the message is straightforward: Current agreements remain in place through their existing terms, but now is the time to understand the changes and begin planning for future renewals.


### A New Era for Microsoft 365 Education A7


**Microsoft 365 Education A7** is now generally available for institutions prepared to scale AI securely across teaching, learning, research, and administration. A7 builds on the advanced protection and governance foundation of Microsoft 365 Education A5 and adds Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Agent 365, Microsoft Intune Suite, and Microsoft Entra Suite in one integrated platform.


The value extends beyond features. A5 helps institutions secure identities, devices, applications, and data; manage compliance; and respond to threats. A7 extends that foundation by putting Copilot into the flow of work, grounding AI experiences in institution-aware knowledge through Work IQ and providing a control plane to observe, secure, and govern agents at scale. Together, these capabilities can improve student outcomes, expand educator capacity, automate processes, and scale AI confidently.


A7 is not an automatic upgrade for every user. It is best suited to institutions with defined AI priorities, high-value use cases, an adoption plan, appropriate security and governance maturity, and a need to manage AI agents across the organization. Connection can help evaluate where A7 can deliver measurable value and where A2, A3, or A5 may be a better fit.


### More Choice Across Faculty and Student Needs


Education technology is not one-size-fits-all. The updated lineup includes Microsoft 365 Education A0, A2, A3, A5, and A7, allowing institutions to assign different editions to faculty and student populations based on actual requirements. Paid editions are available with or without Teams where offered, providing flexibility for institutions that use another collaboration platform or learning management system.


Microsoft 365 Education A0 is a new student-only offer available at no additional cost for eligible institutions beginning January 1, 2028. To qualify, an institution must license all faculty users with A2 or higher, eligible students must use Windows devices for educational purposes, and the institution may receive up to 20 A0 student licenses for each eligible paid faculty license. A0 includes Office desktop and Web apps, Minecraft Education, OneDrive, and Entra ID Free, but it does not include Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Teams, Microsoft Classroom, or a contribution to pooled tenant storage. It should be viewed as a foundational option, not a direct replacement for the Student Use Benefit.


### Teaching and Learning Are Evolving Too


Microsoft Classroom is a purpose-built education experience planned for Microsoft 365 Education A2 through A7. It brings together Assignments, Classwork, Class Notebook, Gradebook, Learning Accelerators, Reflect, Education Insights, School Data Sync, and AI-assisted workflows. It helps educators personalize learning, identify needs earlier, streamline tasks, and connect learning and feedback.


Microsoft Classroom complements rather than replaces Teams or an institution’s LMS. Through Microsoft 365 integrations and Microsoft 365 LTI, institutions can connect learning and AI experiences to the environments educators and students already use.


### Storage and Legacy Offers Require Planning


Beginning January 1, 2028, the current 100TB base tenant quota will be removed at the customer’s next renewal, while storage will remain pooled at the tenant level. Entitlements will be calculated from licensed users. Paid student licenses will contribute storage for the first time: A2 contributes 4GB per student, A3 contributes 8GB, and A5 or A7 contributes 12GB. Faculty contributions increase to 50GB for A2, 75GB for A3, and 150GB for A5 or A7. A0 contributes no storage, although A0 users can consume storage from the institution’s pool.


Institutions should model current consumption, projected enrollment, faculty counts, and the planned license mix well before renewal. Depending on the result, options may include adjusting the license mix, reducing consumption, purchasing additional storage, or archiving inactive content with Microsoft 365 Archive.


Legacy offers also require attention. Office 365 A1 reaches partner-channel end of sale on May 1, 2027 and retires January 1, 2028. The Student Use Benefit and free Exchange Online for Alumni also retire January 1, 2028. At an institution’s first renewal or extension on or after that date, affected users who need continued service must move to an eligible replacement. Existing agreements, licenses, entitlements, and pricing remain in effect through the end of the current term.


### Prepare Today for What’s Next in Education


Every institution’s path forward will look different. Renewal timing, licensing models, faculty and student needs, Windows-device eligibility, storage consumption, security maturity, collaboration choices, and AI priorities will all shape the right approach.


Rather than waiting for renewal to address these changes, institutions can use this time to assess their current environment, understand potential impacts, and build a transition strategy aligned to future goals.

These changes are more than a licensing transition. They’re an opportunity to create a more secure, flexible, integrated, and AI-ready foundation for the future of education.

### Microsoft 365 Education Changes: Frequently Asked Questions


**1. When will the Microsoft 365 Education changes affect my institution?**
Timing will depend on the specific change and your institution’s agreement and renewal schedule. Several major transitions take effect beginning **January 1, 2028** , including the retirement of Office 365 A1 and the Student Use Benefit. Existing agreements, licenses, entitlements, and pricing remain in effect through the end of the current term.


**2. What is Microsoft 365 Education A7, and how is it different from A5?**
Microsoft 365 Education A7 builds on the security, compliance, and governance foundation of A5 by adding capabilities such as **Microsoft 365 Copilot, Microsoft Agent 365, Microsoft Intune Suite, and Microsoft Entra Suite** . It is designed for institutions looking to securely operationalize AI, put Copilot into the flow of work, and govern AI agents at scale.


**3. What will replace Office 365 A1 and the Student Use Benefit?**
Microsoft is expanding its education lineup with options including **A0, A2, A3, A5, and A7** . A0 will provide a no-additional-cost option for eligible students using Windows devices, subject to specific faculty licensing and eligibility requirements. Because A0 does not include all the services available through previous programs, institutions should evaluate which offering best fits each user population.


**4. How will the new Microsoft 365 Education storage model affect our institution?**
Beginning with applicable renewals on or after **January 1, 2028** , Microsoft will remove the current 100TB base tenant quota and calculate pooled storage based on licensed users. Paid student licenses will contribute storage for the first time, while faculty licenses will provide different storage contributions depending on the edition. Institutions should assess current utilization and future requirements before renewal.


**5. How can Connection help us prepare for these Microsoft 365 Education changes?**
Connection can help assess your existing Microsoft 365 Education environment, review your licensing mix, model storage and licensing scenarios, identify transition risks, evaluate the appropriate Microsoft 365 Education offerings, and build an AI-ready roadmap. Your Connection Account Team can also help you **explore available offers based on your institution’s eligibility** as part of the planning process.
